summary: Treat bare mgarvne? as an unresolved editorial query, not a second attested example.
rationale: No translation, citation or context accompanies this fragment. Preserve the text as a question; the securely attested example is the preceding mgarvne quotation.

summary: example for sense 1 in Part. Pass. (MAC Ishaq Material culture/92)

data.turoyo: Quṭʕiwa qayso yarixo, taqriban ʕaṣro+sanṭime ḥlimo, mnaǧríwayle mgarvno, tre ŭ falge, tloṯo yurxo, lo+g̊forəq.
data.translation: They would cut a long log, approximately 10 centimetres thick, fashion (lit. ‘carpenter’) it round, two and a half, three (meters) in length, it doesn’t matter.

rationale: Thin existing Part. Pass. cell; rounded shaft as result complement of carpentry.

summary: example for sense 1 in Part. Pass. (MAC Ishaq Material culture/96)

data.turoyo: Annaqqa lu+nirano kətle bu+falgàyḏeste qayso mgarvno, xud i+dayira.
data.translation: Now then, this yoke has, in its middle, too, a round piece of wood, like a ring.

rationale: Thin existing Part. Pass. cell; attributive rounded part, explicitly compared to a ring.

summary: example for sense 1 in Part. Pass. (MAC Ishaq old houses/5)

data.turoyo: Ánnaqqa saymiwa bayto manək… e, hawxa, mdawṛno, mgaṛvno, bu+šəklano. Kowele tarʕo, bas hiye kulle kéfeyo, xdi+qubo hawxa.
data.translation: Then they used to make one of those houses ... yes, like so, circular, round, in that shape. Apart from a door, it was entirely stones, like a dome.

rationale: Existing Part. Pass. box already covers mgarvno; add a clear rounded-house context there rather than create a duplicate Detransitive box.

summary: The entry already contains Part. Pass. under stem I; its raw Pass. Ptc. heading is the same category. New Detransitive Part. Pass. proposals do not establish a new box.

Retained the inherited stem I label and mgarvalle/mgarvən base forms. The headword comments on the derivation from round; m-initial quadriliteral shape alone does not justify changing the stem system.
Mgarvno modifies houses, a shaped shaft and a ring-like yoke part; plural mgarvne occurs for kiln construction. These are rounded result states or attributes, not new shape-specific senses.
Source mgaṛvno retains ṛ in additions. Comparison with mdawrno/mdawrne and the inherited uncertainty over -ne is noted without normalising either spelling.
The existing Part. Pass. raw count includes one unreferenced question fragment; only one inherited example is securely attested. No new idiom is supported.
Is the intended stem designation I or Q? Keep I until the editors resolve the inherited paradigm filing.
Are mgarvno/mgarvne productive Part. Pass. forms or lexical shape adjectives, and is plural -ne influenced by mdawrne as the inherited note suggests?
Does MlfI_Houses2/81 map to MAC Ishaq Material culture/78? The quotation is identical; citation replacement needs a mapping.
